inputs.source: SSO-authenticated chat message from the employee
Published HR policy index content, maintained by the HR content team with two-person review before publishing

instructions.note: The only safeguard against the agent giving legal advice is a prompt instruction, with no structural backstop such as a topic classifier. A more capable or adversarially prompted model could rationalize an exception, though the consequence is limited since no consequential capability is involved.

elements.name: Employee question into the agent via SSO-authenticated chat
Policy content read by the agent from the index
Chat reply returned to the same authenticated session

controls.name: Read-only credential scoped to the policy index
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the credential/IAM layer outside the model; the agent cannot act outside this scope regardless of model capability or prompting.

controls.name: Network-layer egress denial, verified by penetration test
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced at the network layer outside the model and verified by pen test; holds regardless of model behavior or prompting, so it does not decay with capability.

controls.name: Model pinned; version change requires a change ticket
controls.decay_rationale: The pin itself does not decay; it gates the model_upgrade trigger behind a change-management process rather than allowing a silent capability jump.

controls.name: Two-person review required to publish to the policy index
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced in the HR content publishing workflow, outside the agent and the model; a manipulated agent cannot write to the index regardless of its behavior.

controls.name: Chat client does not render images or auto-fetch links
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the chat client, not the model; closes a covert rendering or auto-fetch side channel regardless of what the model outputs.

controls.name: Prompt instruction: do not give legal advice
controls.decay_rationale: Relies entirely on the model choosing to follow the instruction; a more capable or adversarially prompted model could rationalize exceptions.

controls.name: Attributable audit log of agent queries and replies
controls.decay_rationale: Would be enforced by a logging or audit store outside the model; currently absent from the declared design.

controls.name: Per-user rate limit or step cap on queries
controls.decay_rationale: Would be enforced by the runtime or gateway outside the model; currently absent from the declared design.

findings.title: No attributable record of agent queries and replies (missing audit trail)

forecast.watch_signal: Tool manifest or MCP config diff adds a capability with action write, delete, execute, spend, delegate, or credential_access, without an accompanying audit log being added at the same time.

evidence.observation: Runtime notes describe credential scope, egress denial, and model pinning, but do not mention any logging or audit record of the questions the agent receives or the replies it sends.

recommendations.action: Add an append-only, tamper-evident log recording each employee question and agent reply, attributable to the authenticated session, enforced independent of model output.

findings.title: No rate, step, or cost limit on agent queries (missing resource-exhaustion control)

forecast.watch_signal: A spend-incurring, execute, or external API tool is added, or median queries per session rises well beyond normal interactive chat use.

evidence.observation: Autonomy is declared as A3 with no max_unattended_steps or max_runtime_minutes stated, and no rate or spend cap is described for policy_search.search or chat replies.

recommendations.action: Add a per-session or per-user rate limit on policy_search.search calls and chat replies, enforced outside the model.

stride_coverage.rationale: Single first-party agent operating behind an SSO-authenticated chat client; no external party can present itself as this agent within the design described.
Single-tenant, organization-wide published HR policy content of internal sensitivity only; there is no cross-tenant or cross-user retrieval boundary to leak across.
Artifacts do not describe query volume limits or resource protections on the policy index itself, only that the agent's own credential to it is read-only.
Employee identity is established by the organization's SSO before the chat session reaches the agent; impersonating the employee is an identity-provider concern outside this agent's design.

rating.rationale: The design has no untrusted input: the employee question comes through an authenticated SSO channel (trusted) and the only content source is an HR-maintained, two-person-reviewed policy index (internal). Both capabilities are read-only or reply-only, stay within the organization's trust boundary, and have no egress (network egress denial is verified by pen test), so inherent and residual risk from attack paths are low. The two findings are property gaps, not attack paths: no attributable audit log of agent activity, and no rate or step cap on queries. Because every affected capability is non-consequential today (read and reply only), both are rated low per the rubric's property-finding rule. The forecast is driven entirely by these two gaps: if a new_tool or data_scope_expansion trigger adds a consequential capability (write, delete, execute, spend, delegate, or credential access) without also adding logging or a rate/spend cap, the same missing properties would then cover a materially more consequential action, raising the projected tier to moderate. No single declared control's decay drives this; it is the combination of two structural controls that do not yet exist.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts (system prompt, tool manifest, and runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior.

No MCP configuration or infrastructure-as-code was provided; the egress-denial, credential-scoping, and two-person-review claims are taken from the runtime notes as declared or stated-verified, and were not independently re-verified by this assessment.
No logging or audit architecture was described in any artifact; its absence is inferred from silence in the artifacts, which may understate what actually exists in the runtime.
